text:
- [RARC.5.2.4] **TTL bookkeeping.** `ttl` facts carry a deadline, and a
  fact whose deadline is at or before the engine clock is **expired**: a fact
  due at the current instant does not survive it. A pump retracts every expired
  `ttl` fact at its entry, before the agenda runs ([NTST.3.4]). Retraction is
  ordered: each TTL retraction reaches the stream with its own `seq`.

idris.name: rarc_5_2_4__agree_away_from_boundary
idris.note: The two readings agree away from the boundary: strictly before the deadline neither expires the fact, strictly after both do. An implementation choosing either behaves identically at every instant except one, so only a fixture that lands exactly on a deadline can pin the clause's reading.

idris.name: rarc_5_2_4__expired_exclusive
idris.note: "Expired" read EXCLUSIVELY: the fact survives the instant it is due. THE REFUSED READING; partial because it models a reading the clause does not admit.

idris.name: rarc_5_2_4__expired_inclusive
idris.note: "Expired" read INCLUSIVELY: a fact whose deadline is at or before the clock is expired. THE CLAUSE'S READING: what both runtimes implement, the differential harness validates, lfac.k sweeps by and Rete/TtlSweep.idr takes, and what RARC.5.6.3 states in so many words, 'at or before the monotonic sample'.

idris.name: rarc_5_2_4__readings_differ_only_at_the_deadline
idris.note: The two readings disagree exactly ON the boundary, deadline equal to now: the one instant the clause's inclusive reading decides. Under it the fact is expired here; under the refused one it survives. It names the instant a fixture must land on.

tla.name: rarc_5_2_4__Tick
tla.note: One tick is one clock sample and the pump that follows it: every live answer ages by one, and each whose age has reached its TTL is expired, inclusively, and retracted at the pump's entry in the same step; a cooled call's cooldown window elapses by one as well. The ordering of the retractions and their `seq` are not modelled.
